The pass@k plots extend to k=1000, but the paper never reports the corresponding number of generations, even though its estimator section requires n at least 2k and the evaluation section otherwise specifies only 32 samples. Small benchmark sizes, absent confidence intervals, and no repeated training seeds further prevent judging statistical robustness, especially for the smaller ablation and out-of-domain gains.

Reproducibility is inadequate: the advertised code/data/model URL is blank; exact filtering heuristics, retained set sizes at each curriculum stage, answer-verifier implementation, checkpoint selection, runtime, and several large-k evaluation details are missing.

Novelty is limited. Several interpretations overstate or contradict the presented evidence. Figure 5's entropy falls markedly after its early peak despite being described as increasing or stable; evaluation on the 26K training prompts is presented as evidence of generalization; tiny cross-domain gains lack uncertainty estimates; and the text claims to surpass the 32B model across all benchmarks even though its AIME24 score is slightly lower.
